title: AiDB
introParagraph: AiDB turns Excel files into fully queryable online datasets, letting users explore their data using SQL or plain English prompts translated by generative AI (OpenAI API integration). I built AiDB because I noticed small businesses, research groups, students, and teams using Excel to store their data then struggle when their files grow too large or they want to understand the data they have. With AI advancements, people no longer need a technical background to safely and easily work with databases, and AiDB was designed to make that possible.
bodyParagraph1: The frontend is built with React and MUI, providing a user-friendly interface for both SQL and AI-driven queries. Natural-language prompts are translated into SQL through the AI, which only generates queries; all SQL is validated and executed safely against the user's own data. The backend is Java Spring Boot and combines Firebase for authentication, Firestore for business data, AWS EC2 for hosting, and AWS RDS for relational storage.
bodyParagraph2: One of the core engineering challenges was balancing query flexibility with strict data isolation. All tables and records are stored under hashed internal identifiers and accessed only through an internal mapping layer, so users cannot enumerate, reference, or join data outside their own datasets. Another part of AiDB's backend that required careful planning was preparing the system for sharding and multiple database instances in the future. To do this, I used Snowflake IDs to ensure globally unique entity identifiers across databases, avoiding collisions and supporting scalable multi-DB deployments.
bodyParagraph3: To deploy AiDB, I built a CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions that automates the process of deploying my application to both my sandbox and production environments. I hosted the frontend on Firebase for easy user management, while AWS provides the isolated compute and relational database layer. The business logic is fully covered by 200+ automated tests, and a smoke test is conducted for each environment during deployment.
conclusionParagraph: AiDB is an ongoing effort. My planned features are paid subscription tiers, a tutorial/sandbox environment, and qualitative data analysis. In the future, I also plan on adding API integrations to popular business data sites like Square and Jobber so that users can link their accounts and pull in their data with the click of a button.
conclusionParagraph2: Check out AiDB in action at askaidb.com!
